result.title: JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces
result.summary: LLM agents generate intermediate reasoning and actions token by token, making extended interactions slow and computationally expensive. Jev-style models offer fast probabilistic predictions over finite fields, but require those fields to be specified in advance. This requirement limits autonomous task solving, where the available actions must be derived from natural language instructions and adapted through interaction. We introduce JevSpawn, a compositional policy that connects natural language task specifications to finite probabilistic exploration. Parallel action spawning is coupled with feedback driven branch selection, representation revision, and recovery from retained alternatives. Shared action structure and model prefixes reduce repeated generation and context computation without additional training. Evaluations on eight benchmark tasks against seven agent baselines and a TypeSafe Jev variant establish JevSpawn as a promising approach to structured agentic inference, with improved task performance and faster navigation.

AI.brief_summary: JevSpawn 提出一种组合式策略，把自然语言任务说明映射为有限域上的概率探索，通过并行「动作孵化」配合反馈驱动的分支选择、表示修订与备选恢复，在不额外训练的前提下复用前缀与共享动作结构以减少重复生成与上下文计算，并在八个基准任务上对比七种 agent 基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其并行分支生成、反馈驱动的表示修订与保留备选恢复机制，可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态更新、候选假设筛选和停止/回退决策的问题表述相关，可供核查是否可迁移到推理期状态管理；但论文面向文本 agent，视觉与 latent 表示证据未涉及。
